To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Epstein-Barr virus gene expression was detected by in situ hybridization in 65% of lung biopsies from HIV-infected children with chronic pulmonary diseases, but without significant association of the disease with PLH/LI complex.

EBV gene expression in lung tissue samples of Brazilian HIV-1 infected patients was detected in the vast majority of cases but without significant association to PLH/LIP or to the T-cell and B-cell response.
Epstein-Barr virus gene expression was detected by ISH in the majority of lung tissue sections of HIV-1 infected Brazilian children with chronic lung diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the association between EBV and PLH/LIP in HIV-1-infected children.
the possible role of Epstein-Barr virus infection in the pathogenesis or in the progression of pulmonary disease in HIV- 1-infected children.
the possible role of Epstein-Barr virus in the development of lung disease in Brazilian HIV-1-infected children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PLH/LIP is not associated to EBV infection, and that the EBV detection in the lung tissue is probably due to the high number of T cells and B cells present in the lesions.
EBV gene expression is not associated with PLH/Lip complex, but the role of EBV as an important pathogenetic factor in the pathogenesis remains to be elucidated.
EBV gene expression is not associated with PLH/LI in HIV-1-infected children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBV gene expression is not associated with PLH/LP in Brazilian HIV-1-infected children.

the presence of EBV gene expression in lung tissue samples of HIV-infected children with PLH/LI complex is not associated with the presence of PLH/LI, but the presence of T-lymphocyte subsets in lung tissue is significantly associated with the presence and the pattern of PLH/LH.
the presence of EBV gene expression in lung tissue samples is not related to the histological diagnosis of PLH/LI, but to a more severe pulmonary disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EBV is present in most of the lung samples, but it is not associated to PLH/LIP or to the TCD4+, CD8+, and B cell counts.
EBV gene expression in HIV-1-infected children with chronic pulmonary diseases is not necessarily associated with PLH/Lip.
EBV gene expression is not associated with PLH/LI in Brazilian children with chronic lung diseases.
